title: Data stored without encryption
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB without encryption at rest, risking unauthorized access if the database is compromised.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB is not configured with encryption at rest by default.
uncertainty_note: Encryption status of MongoDB instance not specified; threat assumes common default configurations.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Video Data
description: Video metadata and files stored in MongoDB (DS3) may be accessible to unauthorized parties if encryption at rest or access controls are insufficient.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 lacks robust encryption or access control mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Node id D.1.1 is based on common LINDDUN Pro structure; exact node may vary by version.

title: Identifiability via Metadata
description: Video metadata (e.g., timestamps, user IDs) stored in DS3 could allow linking videos to specific individuals if not anonymized.
assumptions: Assumes metadata contains direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id I.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN Pro taxonomy; verify against specific tree.

title: Secondary Use of Video Data
description: Video Management Service (P2) may store or process video data for purposes beyond user consent (e.g., analytics, profiling).
assumptions: Assumes lack of purpose limitation controls in P2.
uncertainty_note: Node id Dd.1.1 is approximate; confirm with LINDDUN Pro threat tree.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Laws
description: Storing video data without explicit consent or legal basis may violate regulations like GDPR.
assumptions: Assumes video data is considered personal data under applicable laws.
uncertainty_note: Node id Nc.1.1 is a general placeholder; specific compliance nodes may differ.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: Child browsing data transmitted from MongoDB to AI engine may be intercepted if not encrypted, leading to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without encryption or with weak security measures.

title: Re-identification of Children via Browsing Data
description: AI engine may link browsing patterns to specific children using identifiers or inference, compromising anonymity.
assumptions: Browsing data contains or can be correlated with unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, user profiles).

title: Lack of Informed Consent for Data Processing
description: Children/guardians may not be aware their browsing data is collected and sent to AI engine for profiling.
assumptions: No explicit consent mechanism or transparency about data usage is implemented.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: AI engine processing may violate regulations like COPPA if child data is used without parental consent or safeguards.
assumptions: AI engine lacks compliance checks for child-specific legal requirements.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Government ID Images
description: Sensitive government ID images stored in the file system could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls or encryption are insufficient.
assumptions: File system lacks proper access controls or encryption for stored data.

title: Data Linkable to Individuals
description: Government ID images inherently contain personally identifiable information, enabling direct linkage to specific individuals if exposed.
assumptions: Data is stored without anonymization or pseudonymization.

title: Individuals Unaware of Data Processing
description: Users may not be informed that their government ID images are being stored, violating transparency principles.
assumptions: No explicit consent or notification mechanism is in place for data storage.

title: Potential Non-Compliance with Legal Requirements
description: Storing government ID images may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR) if not handled with appropriate safeguards.
assumptions: Jurisdiction-specific legal requirements for handling government IDs are not fully addressed.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on specific regional laws and implementation details.

title: JWT Exposure via Insecure Storage
description: Storing JWT in browser localStorage without encryption allows potential access via XSS attacks, leading to unauthorized disclosure of authentication tokens and user session hijacking.
assumptions: Assumes no additional client-side protections (e.g., Content Security Policy) are in place to mitigate XSS risks.
uncertainty_note: Node D.1.1 is selected based on insecure storage disclosure; D.2.1 (lack of encryption) could also apply but D.1.1 is more directly tied to storage location risks.
